title: Root subgroups generate smooth connected overgroups of a maximal torus
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Smoothness, connectedness and finite type mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful finite-dimensional representation. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a split maximal torus: a closed subgroup [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\geq0$ and maximal among torus subgroups, with $\mathbf G_m$ as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. Write $X^*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{F\text{-grp}}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and let $\Phi\subseteq X^*(T)\setminus\{0\}$ be the nonzero character weights of $T$ acting by conjugation on the tangent space $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ at $1$. For each $\alpha\in\Phi$, let $U_\alpha\subseteq G$ be the smooth connected root subgroup with $\operatorname{Lie}(U_\alpha)=\operatorname{Lie}(G)_\alpha$ supplied by [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Let $H\subseteq G$ be any smooth connected closed subgroup containing $T$, and put $\Phi_H=\{\alpha\in\Phi:\operatorname{Lie}(H)_\alpha\ne0\}$. Then $U_\alpha\subseteq H$ if and only if $\alpha\in\Phi_H$, and $H$ is the smallest closed subgroup scheme of $G$ containing $T$ and all $U_\alpha$ with $\alpha\in\Phi_H$. Explicitly, every closed subgroup scheme $J\subseteq G$ containing those subgroup schemes also contains $H$; no smoothness or connectedness is required of $J$. These are inclusions of subgroup schemes and thus hold as inclusions of functors on all commutative $F$-algebras. Neither reductivity nor parabolicity is required of $H$. Every characteristic and the empty root set are allowed.

source.place: Milne 21.66, printed p.444, with H containing T; the root-containment criterion is stated there using 21.11(c), and the generation assertion is its final sentence (using 10.17).

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ and $\mathfrak t=\operatorname{Lie}(T)$. Since $T\subseteq H$, conjugation by $T$ preserves $H$: for every $F$-algebra $A$, $t h t^{-1}\in H(A)$ for $t\in T(A)$ and $h\in H(A)$, by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. By [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], the inclusion on tangent vectors sends a dual-number point to the same point in $G$; it is injective because subgroup inclusions are injective on all algebra points. Its linearity and compatibility with composition are supplied by [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus]. Differentiating conjugation therefore makes $\mathfrak h$ a $T$-stable vector subspace of $\mathfrak g$, containing $\mathfrak t$. The group $H$ is affine of finite type: if $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$, then $H=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and the images of any finite algebra generators of $A$ generate $A/I$.

source.place: 21.66, printed p.444; Theorem 21.11(b),(c), pp.428--430; Proposition 16.64, pp.348--349; Corollary 10.17, p.191.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-trivial-torus-coherent-weight-decomposition] on $\operatorname{Spec}F$ to the finite-dimensional representation $\mathfrak h$ (a coherent module on the Noetherian one-point scheme). Its weight summands map into the corresponding summands of $\mathfrak g$: an equivariant inclusion sends a vector with character $\chi$ to a vector with the same character. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $\mathfrak g_0=\mathfrak t$, the nonzero weights form the finite set $\Phi$, and every $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ is one-dimensional. Since $\mathfrak t\subseteq\mathfrak h$, its zero summand is exactly $\mathfrak t$; every other nonzero summand equals the ambient line. Thus $$\mathfrak h=\mathfrak t\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_H}\mathfrak g_\alpha.$$ This uses character weights rather than differentials of characters, including in positive characteristic.

source.place: 21.66, printed p.444; Theorem 21.11(b),(c), pp.428--430; Proposition 16.64, pp.348--349; Corollary 10.17, p.191.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha\in\Phi$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], the only roots rationally proportional to $\alpha$ are $\alpha,-\alpha$, so the positive-ray space $V_\alpha$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ is exactly $\mathfrak g_\alpha$. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-positive-ray-subgroup] to conjugation by $T$ on $G$. Its smooth connected $T$-stable subgroup with tangent space $V_\alpha$ is $U_\alpha$, by the uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. If $\alpha\in\Phi_H$, Step 2 gives $V_\alpha=\mathfrak g_\alpha\subseteq\mathfrak h$, and the positive-ray containment assertion, with $K=H$, gives $U_\alpha\subseteq H$. All its hypotheses hold: $H$ is smooth connected closed and $T$-stable; no reductivity of $H$ is used. Conversely, if $U_\alpha\subseteq H$, the tangent inclusion puts its nonzero tangent line $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ in $\mathfrak h$, so $\alpha\in\Phi_H$.

source.place: 21.66, printed p.444; Theorem 21.11(b),(c), pp.428--430; Proposition 16.64, pp.348--349; Corollary 10.17, p.191.

proof.text: Let $J\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup scheme containing $T$ and the $U_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in\Phi_H$. Put $K=H\times_GJ$. Explicitly, for ideals $I_H,I_J\subseteq A=\mathcal O(G)$, $K=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(I_H+I_J))$, a closed subscheme of $H$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its algebra points are $H(A')\cap J(A')$ for every $F$-algebra $A'$, so it is a subgroup by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]; every specified generator factors through it. The family consisting of $T$ and the finitely many $U_\alpha\subseteq H$ is smooth and connected: use [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus] for $T$ and [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] for the root groups. Their tangent spaces span $\mathfrak h$ by Step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation] with ambient group $H$ and containing subgroup $K$. It yields $K=H$ without requiring $K$ to be smooth or connected. In affine ideals this says $I_H+I_J=I_H$, hence $I_J\subseteq I_H$ and $H\subseteq J$ as subgroup schemes.

source.place: 21.66, printed p.444; Theorem 21.11(b),(c), pp.428--430; Proposition 16.64, pp.348--349; Corollary 10.17, p.191.

proof.text: Step 3 shows that $H$ itself contains all the claimed generators; Step 4 shows it lies in every closed subgroup containing them, proving the asserted minimality. If $\Phi_H$ is empty, the family in Step 4 is still the singleton $\{T\}$ and Step 2 says $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak t$, so the argument is unchanged. In particular it covers $\Phi=\varnothing$ and rank zero. All factorizations above are morphisms of subgroup schemes; evaluating them on any commutative $F$-algebra gives the stated functor inclusions. No hypothesis on $J$ beyond closed subgroup was introduced.

lean.statement: theorem maximal_torus_overgroup_root_generation {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (G T : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (hG : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsReductive G) (iT : T ⟶ G) (hT : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsMaximalTorus iT) (hsplit : ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (T ≅ MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F r)) (aG : ModObj T.X G.X) (haG : aG.smul = adjointMap iT) (U : roots T G aG → Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (iU : ∀ α : roots T G aG, U α ⟶ G) (hU : ∀ α : roots T G aG, IsClosedSubgroupScheme (iU α).hom.hom ∧ Smooth (U α).X.hom ∧ ConnectedSpace (U α).X.left ∧ @TorusCharacterTangent.IsStable F _ T G aG _ (iU α) ∧ (GrpObj.differential (iU α).hom.hom).toLinearMap.range = weight T G aG α.val) (H : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (iH : H ⟶ G) (hHclosed : IsClosedSubgroupScheme iH.hom.hom) (hHsmooth : Smooth H.X.hom) (hHconn : ConnectedSpace H.X.left) (jT : T ⟶ H) (hjT : jT ≫ iH = iT) (aH : ModObj T.X H.X) (haH : aH.smul = adjointMap jT) : (∀ α : roots T G aG, (∃ f : U α ⟶ H, f ≫ iH = iU α) ↔ weight T H aH α.val ≠ ⊥) ∧ ∀ (J : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (iJ : J ⟶ G), IsClosedSubgroupScheme iJ.hom.hom → (∃ f : T ⟶ J, f ≫ iJ = iT) → (∀ α : roots T G aG, weight T H aH α.val ≠ ⊥ → ∃ f : U α ⟶ J, f ≫ iJ = iU α) → ∃ f : H ⟶ J, f ≫ iJ = iH
